mechanism_claims.claim_text: PG-1 cytotoxicity in the mammalian cell panel correlates with cell-dependent beta-sheet/conformational changes observed by circular dichroism after interaction with cells; this supports a membrane-interaction mechanism but does not prove a receptor-specific target.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: recombinant PG-1 in mammalian cell panel

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=5:The magnitude of AMP folding determines the level of PG-1 cytotoxicity in mammalian cells

mechanism_claims.limitations: The claim is correlation/biophysical interaction evidence; it is not an intracellular target assay.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Cell-surface negative charge/sulfated proteoglycan context modulates PG-1-associated toxicity: positively charged GFP internalization differs by cell type and sodium chlorate treatment reduces GFP internalization while increasing viability after AMP exposure, especially in 661W cells.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: PG-1, PMAP-36, melittin comparison in 661W and NIH-3T3 charge-perturbation context

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=6:The magnitude of the positive charges on GFP determines the degree of membrane penetration and the level of mammalian cell cytotoxicity
source_locator.secondary_locator: xml:sec=7:A reduction in the negative charge on the cell membrane results in a decrease in the mammalian cell cytotoxicity of PG-1

mechanism_claims.limitations: Supported as a charge/context phenotype, not as a single closed molecular target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: SEM imaging shows membrane/cell-surface damage and lysis-like morphology after PG-1 treatment in high- and low-susceptibility mammalian cell lines, supporting membrane disruption/cell rupture as a direct damage phenotype.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=8:Comparison of scanning electron microscopic images between cells showing high (661W) and low (NIH-3T3) cytotoxicity to PG-1

mechanism_claims.limitations: SEM supports membrane/cell damage morphology but does not quantify pore formation in these mammalian cells.

caution_findings.note: Claims are limited to CD/charge/SEM-supported membrane-interaction phenotypes; no receptor-specific or intracellular target mechanism is asserted.
